what_its_for: Fosamprenavir is used to treat HIV (Human Immunodeficiency Virus) infection in adults and children. It belongs to a group of medicines called protease inhibitors. It works by blocking an enzyme that HIV needs to make copies of itself, which helps lower the amount of HIV in your blood and keeps your immune system stronger. It is always used together with other HIV medicines — never alone.
how_to_take: Take fosamprenavir exactly as your doctor tells you. You can take the tablets with or without food. If you take the oral suspension (liquid), adults should take it without food on an empty stomach. Children can take the liquid with food. Swallow the tablets whole with a full glass of water. If you are using the liquid, shake the bottle well before each use and measure your dose carefully with the measuring device provided. Do not use a household spoon, as it may not give you the correct amount. Always take fosamprenavir as part of a combination HIV treatment plan with other antiviral medicines.
dosing: Your doctor will decide the right dose for you based on your weight, age, other medicines you take (especially ritonavir, which is often given together with fosamprenavir to boost its effect), and your kidney or liver health. A common adult dose is 1,400 mg twice daily without ritonavir, or 700 mg twice daily with ritonavir 100 mg. Do not change your dose or stop taking this medicine without talking to your doctor first.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember — but only if it is not too close to the time of your next scheduled dose. If it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at the regular time. Never take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one. Missing doses can allow the virus to grow and become harder to treat, so try to take your medicine at the same times every day.
storage: Store fosamprenavir tablets at room temperature, between 59°F and 86°F (15°C to 30°C). Keep the tablets in their original container and away from moisture, heat, and direct light. Store the oral suspension (liquid) in the refrigerator or at room temperature — do not freeze it. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Do not use this medicine after the expiration date printed on the label. Ask your pharmacist how to safely dispose of any unused medicine.
what_to_avoid: Do not take certain medicines while using fosamprenavir, as they can cause serious or life-threatening problems. These include some cholesterol medicines (like lovastatin and simvastatin), certain migraine medicines (like ergotamine), some sedatives (like triazolam and oral midazolam), rifampin (an antibiotic), St. John's Wort (an herbal supplement), and certain other HIV medicines. Always tell every doctor, dentist, and pharmacist about ALL medicines, vitamins, and supplements you take before starting fosamprenavir. Avoid drinking large amounts of alcohol. Do not stop taking your HIV medicines without your doctor's approval, even if you feel fine.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or seek emergency care if you experience: a severe skin rash, blisters, or peeling skin; yellowing of your skin or eyes (signs of liver problems); severe stomach pain, nausea, or vomiting; signs of high blood sugar such as increased thirst or urination; unusual bleeding or bruising; changes in body fat distribution (such as fat buildup in your belly, neck, or breasts, or thinning in your arms, legs, or face); signs of an immune system reaction (fever, swollen glands, rash) as your immune system recovers. Also talk to your doctor if you develop new or worsening symptoms of any kind.
when_it_works: Fosamprenavir starts working soon after you take it, but you may not feel any different at first. HIV medicines work over time — your doctor will check your viral load (amount of HIV in the blood) and CD4 cell count (immune cell count) with regular blood tests to see how well the medicine is working. It is important to keep taking your medicine every day as prescribed, even when you feel healthy, because stopping can allow the virus to multiply and become resistant to treatment. This medicine does not cure HIV or prevent passing it to others.
special_populations: Children: Fosamprenavir is approved for children 4 weeks of age and older. The dose is based on the child's weight. The oral liquid form is often used for younger children. Pregnant women: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. The benefits and risks should be discussed with your healthcare provider. Liver problems: Use with caution if you have liver disease, especially hepatitis B or C. Dose adjustments may be needed for moderate to severe liver problems. Kidney problems: No dose adjustment is usually needed for kidney disease alone, but your doctor will monitor you closely. Older adults: Use with care; your doctor will monitor for any side effects more closely.
